title: Ruy Lopez
intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5, the Spanish Opening: slow, lasting pressure on Black's centre. Played at every level.

lessons.title: The Spanish main line
lessons.summary: Pressure the defender of e5, keep the bishop, castle.

steps.text: The Ruy Lopez starts 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5. The bishop attacks the knight that defends e5.
Play the first three moves of the Ruy Lopez.
steps.hint: e4 and Nf3 as usual, then the bishop goes one square further than in the Italian.
steps.ifWrong: That is playable, but the Ruy Lopez goes e4, Nf3 and Bb5.

steps.text: If the knight on c6 disappeared, e5 would be left undefended. That threat hangs over Black for the whole game.
Black's most popular answer is 3...a6 (the Morphy Defence): it asks the bishop what it wants.
Keep your bishop: step back to a4, staying on the same diagonal.
steps.hint: Retreat along the diagonal towards the a-file.
steps.ifWrong: The main line keeps the bishop with a retreat to a4.
steps.ifRight: The bishop still pins down the knight.

feedback.b5c6: Taking the knight is the Exchange Variation, a fine choice. The main line keeps the bishop.

steps.text: Black develops with 4...Nf6 and attacks e4.
Castle. Your e4 pawn is safe enough for now: if Black takes it, your rook will use the open e-file.
steps.hint: Move the king two squares towards the h1 rook.
steps.ifWrong: Castle now; it is the main line.
steps.ifRight: Castled, with the rook ready for the e-file.

steps.text: Black grabbed the pawn with 5...Nxe4 (the Open Variation). Find a strong reply.
steps.hint: Open the centre while Black's king is still in the middle.
steps.ifWrong: Use your lead in development: open lines towards Black's king.
steps.ifRight: Good: you open lines while Black's king is still in the centre.
